user_request:
Create one content-rich method figure for He et al., Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners, CVPR 2022, grounded in Section 3 of the uploaded official paper. Explain the asymmetric pre-training computation, not results. Preserve the actual mechanism: random non-overlapping patch selection; a ViT encoder sees ONLY visible patch embeddings with positions; encoded visible representations are combined with shared learned mask tokens after the encoder, restored to spatial order and given decoder positions; a small decoder predicts patch pixels; MSE is computed only at masked locations against the original image. A small separate downstream strip may show the pretrained encoder receiving a full image, with no reconstruction decoder. Do not invent metrics, model depths, or a classifier training protocol.

The previous figure failed because it was full of meaningless document icons and anonymous squares. This figure must explain operations with concrete image content. Use one coherent original red bicycle image (side view against a pale wall), recognizable at all stages. A 4 x 4 schematic patch layout is sufficient for legibility: four visible patches at row-major indices 3, 6, 12, 13, twelve masked patches. Show the same retained crops at the same positions, then gather those four actual crops into the encoder. Feature tokens after encoding must be labeled z3, z6, z12, z13, not pretend to be raw image crops. Show one learned mask vector M being repeated into the 12 missing positions AFTER the encoder. The restored decoder sequence/grid must preserve those four indices. A predicted bicycle image and a small aligned target/prediction crop comparison should make the masked-pixel objective concrete. The illustrated predicted image is a schematic, not a benchmark reconstruction result. Do not insert paper figures or fake numerical scores.

Use an open left-to-right computation graph across the upper two-thirds, with a compact masked-loss branch beneath the prediction and a slim downstream reuse strip at bottom left if it fits. Make the sparse input / encoder / full decoder input distinction immediately visible. Input, masked image and predicted image should be large and informative; encoder visually larger than decoder. No row of four explanatory cards, generic page icons, unlabelled token confetti, invented curves, large numbered headings, hero slogan, or long disclaimer. Soft blue for visible features, soft coral for learned mask tokens, green for pixel reconstruction and loss; white background, restrained pastel grouping, crisp dark readable labels. Short label 'Patch layout (schematic)' and small 'He et al. | CVPR 2022' source credit are sufficient.

Write an English drawing prompt of roughly 600-850 words with exact connections and concise labels. Include a short '=== OVERALL COMPOSITION ===' paragraph under 65 words. Preserve source-verified acronym spelling. Any FigureSpec evidence quotes must match the extracted Section 3 text exactly; the illustrated bicycle is a drawing choice, not a claim that the paper used this particular input.
